note: I022 The Captain's Academy: the Captain's Handbook (pages), the First Voyage (steps checked by what the player really does) and the contextual tips (each shown once, linked to a page). Keys are written as {action} and filled in from the game's own key bindings by src/core/academy.gd ({move} is the four move keys, {handbook} F1, {quicksave} F5, {quickload} F9). Coverage: docs/iterations/i022/CAPTAINS_ACADEMY_COVERAGE.md.

pages.title: Controls
pages.text: Walk with {move}. Press {interact} next to something that lights up to use it. {action_wheel} opens the action wheel with what you can do where you stand. {captains_log} opens the Captain's Log, {captains_hat} puts your hat on or takes it off, and {pause} opens the menu (and closes any window). {handbook} opens this Handbook.

pages.title: Your first voyage
pages.text: Go on deck, open the chart, choose a harbour and plan a course, then set sail. Time runs while you sail: the buttons at the top of the screen pause it or make it run 5 or 20 times faster. The boat follows the course by itself; you can sleep, fish or cook on the way, and anything important will stop time and tell you.

pages.title: The action wheel
pages.text: {action_wheel} opens a wheel with what makes sense where you are: in the cabin sleep, the world map, the chart table, provisions, postcards and your little game; on deck the charts, the fishing rod and, underway, the chart plotter, sailing details, radar, sail trim and anchor. On/off items show a check mark.

pages.title: The cabin
pages.text: The cabin has your berth (sleep), the navigation table (the chart), the provisions locker, the work station, the galley stove, the coffee table, the hat hook, the framed world map and the trophy board. Things you can use light up when you are close; press {interact}.

pages.title: Your companion
pages.text: Your cat or dog lives aboard, follows you between cabin and deck and naps where it likes. Walk up and press {interact} to pet it.

pages.title: The Captain's hat
pages.text: {captains_hat} puts the hat on or takes it off. On deck in strong wind it can blow away: the game warns you first, and below deck or ashore it is safe. A lost hat can be replaced at a grocery in harbour.

pages.title: The chart and planning a course
pages.text: Open the chart at the navigation table or from the wheel. Click a harbour (or search for one) and plan a course; drag the course line to add a waypoint, and select a waypoint and press {delete_waypoint} to remove it. The tabs show the course, the weather along it and the details. Zoom with {map_zoom_in} and {map_zoom_out}.

pages.title: Time and speed
pages.text: The world has one clock. The buttons at the top pause time or run it at 1, 5 or 20 times. On long passages a passage panel can run hours per second. Sleeping, working and the pastimes pass hours at once: the screen fades, the clock counts, and you come back at normal speed. Warnings, a fish on the line, the anchor alarm, traffic, a radio call and arriving all stop time early.

pages.title: Underway
pages.text: Set sail from the wheel once a course is planned. The boat sails the course by itself. On deck, {chartplotter} shows the chart plotter, and the wheel offers sailing details and the radar. {sail_trim} opens sail trim: well-trimmed sails are faster.

pages.title: Long passages
pages.text: On long passages the passage panel lets hours pass quickly while the voyage map shows the boat crossing the sea. Everything that would stop time still does.

pages.title: Anchoring
pages.text: Underway, the windlass on the foredeck (or Anchor on the wheel) drops the anchor where the bottom allows. The anchor alarm sounds if it drags. On the chart at the navigation table you can select a waypoint and press {anchorage_key} to make it an anchorage: the boat stops there and asks whether to anchor or sail on.

pages.title: Weather
pages.text: Wind and weather change with time and place; the chart's Weather tab shows what is coming along your course. A weather warning stops fast time and sleep. Strong wind and storms wear the boat and can damage it.

pages.title: Traffic, radar and radio
pages.text: Other ships sail too. If one is on a collision course a warning sounds and the radar opens by itself while the risk lasts. A call on the VHF radio can ask for help or bring a forecast.

pages.title: The boat's condition and rescue
pages.text: The hull, rig and engine wear with miles, time and weather. A boatyard can service and repair them and haul the boat out. If the boat is badly damaged at sea you are rescued and brought to harbour, for a fee.

pages.title: Food and water
pages.text: Food and water are used every day, at sea and in harbour. The provisions locker in the cabin shows how many days are left; buy more at a grocery. The game warns you when stores run low.

pages.title: Harbour services
pages.text: Each harbour offers its own services: a grocery (food, water, a new hat, lures and the fishmonger), a boatyard (boat care, haul-out, chandlery, sailmaker and boats for sale) and Go Ashore. The arrival card says what is there.

pages.title: Boats
pages.text: You start with your first boat. At a boatyard you can buy another boat for its price; boats you own stay yours, and you can move aboard any of them at a boatyard.

pages.title: Money, work and renown
pages.text: In harbour the work station in the cabin offers remote work for pay by the hour. Voyages, new harbours, objectives, postcards and your little game earn renown; publish a travel update in harbour to share it, which also earns a little money.

pages.title: Fishing
pages.text: Set the rod on deck from its holder or the wheel and choose a lure. When a fish bites a bell rings: press {reel_in} and reel it in with good timing. Keep fish in the cool box, release them, sell them at the fishmonger or cook them.

pages.title: The galley and coffee
pages.text: Cook at the galley stove in the cabin; a meal takes a little time. Make coffee, carry the mug, and set it in the cup holder on deck.

pages.title: Sleeping
pages.text: Sleep in the berth for 1 to 12 hours. The world goes on while you sleep, and anything important wakes you.

pages.title: Postcards from the Sea
pages.text: In the cabin, choose Write a postcard on the wheel. Pick what it shows (harbours, catches, your companion, voyages, weather and evening light), the words and the layout, then make and publish it: it takes about two hours. Each subject earns renown once; every card goes in the scrapbook.

pages.title: A Game Developer at Sea
pages.text: In the cabin, choose Work on your little game on the wheel. Pick a task (2 to 4 hours), answer its small question and work; milestones fill the devlog and earn renown, and the release brings the first sales. An interrupted session keeps the hours worked.

pages.title: Making the cabin home
pages.text: Make it home on the cabin's wheel lets you place cabin things you have bought; the framed world map lets you dream of voyages and plan one from it.

pages.title: Saving and loading
pages.text: Open the menu with {pause} to save in one of three slots or load. Aboard, {quicksave} quicksaves and {quickload} loads the quicksave.

pages.title: Difficulty
pages.text: Relaxed, Standard or Seasoned Captain changes starting money, how fast stores are used, wear, weather damage, costs and the rescue fee; the weather itself is the same. Change it any time from the menu: it counts from then on.

pages.title: Settings and tips
pages.text: Settings has the volumes (also the wind on its own), display, interface size and light, language and accessibility. Tips can be turned off there. This Handbook is always here: {handbook} or Captain's Handbook in the menu.

first_voyage.title: The action wheel
first_voyage.text: Press {action_wheel} to open the action wheel. It shows what you can do here. Close it with {pause}.

first_voyage.title: The Captain's Log
first_voyage.text: Press {captains_log} to open the Captain's Log, then close it again.

first_voyage.title: Up on deck
first_voyage.text: Go on deck: walk to the companionway and press {interact}, or choose Go on deck on the wheel.

first_voyage.title: Open the chart
first_voyage.text: Open the chart: Charts on the wheel, or the navigation table in the cabin.

first_voyage.title: Plan a course
first_voyage.text: Click a harbour nearby and plan a course to it.

first_voyage.title: Set sail
first_voyage.text: Go back aboard and choose Set sail on the wheel.

first_voyage.title: Let time run
first_voyage.text: The boat sails the course by itself. Try 5× or 20× at the top of the screen; anything important stops time again.

first_voyage_done.title: Your first voyage
first_voyage_done.text: Well done, Captain: you are on your way. Everything else is in the Captain's Handbook ({handbook}).

cabin.text: Below deck: things that light up can be used with {interact}. The wheel ({action_wheel}) has sleep, provisions, postcards and your little game.

chart.text: The chart: click a harbour to plan a course; drag the line to add a waypoint. The tabs show the weather and the details.

underway.text: Underway! {sail_trim} trims the sails, {chartplotter} shows the chart plotter, and the time buttons at the top make the passage go faster.

arrival.text: In harbour: services differ from port to port. The arrival card said what is here; the work station pays for remote work while moored.

boatyard.text: This harbour has a boatyard: boat care, a chandlery, a sailmaker and boats for sale.

weather.text: A weather warning stops fast time. The chart's Weather tab shows what is coming along the course.

bite.text: A fish on the line: press {reel_in} and reel with good timing.

traffic.text: Traffic: a ship on a collision course. The radar shows it until the risk has passed.

vhf.text: A call on the VHF radio. Help if you can; some calls bring a forecast.

anchor.text: At anchor. If the anchor drags the alarm sounds; the windlass raises it again.

provisions.text: Stores are running low: a grocery in harbour sells food and water.

hat.text: Mind the hat: strong wind on deck can blow it away. {captains_hat} takes it off.

renown.text: Renown earned! Publish a travel update in harbour to share it (the work station or the Captain's Log).

passage.text: A long passage: the passage panel lets hours pass quickly, and the voyage map shows the way.

night.text: Night falls. The berth in the cabin is a fine place to sleep; anything important will wake you.
